vts_boundary_basis: VTS North Sea Canal Area (Port of Amsterdam directive, Q-S9) and the statutory aanloopgebied IJmuiden (Q-S10) are limited to the territorial sea within a 12 nm arc from 52°27.9'N 004°32.1'E. Computed from COLREG.2/Circ.64 coordinates (Q-S12): IJmuiden North vertex (17) 52°31.35'N 004°13.25'E is 11.98 nm from the reference point (on the arc) and all other vertices are 15.4 to 18.7 nm. The TSS therefore lies outside Sector IJmuiden and only touches its boundary. The directive's map shows a wider 'IJmuiden Aanloop' area served by IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7, which is an information-only supporting channel with no defined boundary; whether it is part of the VTS area is not established.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). No Dutch national mandatory reporting system for this area identified: STZ art. 5(1) territorial-sea entry report does not reach it because the TSS lies seaward of the 12 nm IJmuiden arc (Q-S10). The VHF 7 report to IJmuiden Approaches applies to ships bound for IJmuiden and is VTS reporting (Q-S9). Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: IJmuiden North (COLREG.2/Circ.64, implemented 1 Aug 2013) runs NNW from about 12 nm to 18.7 nm off IJmuiden. The statutory VTS North Sea Canal Area and aanloopgebied IJmuiden end at 12 nm; the TSS only touches that arc at one vertex. The IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 information channel extends seaward but its area is not defined in the directive. No IMO or national MRS.
source_date: Q-S9 10 Sep 2025 (in force 30 Sep 2025); Q-S10 version 1 Jan 2025; Q-S12 4 Dec 2012
unresolved_issue: Whether the IJmuiden Approaches (VHF 7) service area is a defined part of VTS North Sea Canal Area and whether it covers the IJmuiden North lanes. Needs the Dutch VTS designation for IJmuiden or ALRS Vol 6 / Dutch Guide to Port Entry diagram.

vts_boundary_basis: IJmuiden West Outer (Q-S12) lies between about 003°54'E and 004°09'E, 14.1 to 15.5 nm and more from the IJmuiden reference point, so outside the 12 nm Sector IJmuiden. The VTS directive scope (a) includes 'the extended IJ-geul deep water channel' and its Appendix I map shows the IJ-geul continuing beyond 12 nm (Q-S9). In Circ.64 the West Outer separation zones are described as lying north and south of the IJmuiden-geul, with the traffic lanes outside them, so the VTS scope includes the deep-water channel the TSS flanks but not demonstrably the TSS lanes or separation zones.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). Seaward of the 12 nm IJmuiden arc, so the STZ art. 5(1) territorial-sea entry report does not apply (Q-S10). VHF 7 report to IJmuiden Approaches is VTS reporting for ships bound to IJmuiden (Q-S9). Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: The TSS flanks the extended IJ-geul beyond 12 nm. The current VTS North Sea Canal Area directive (in force 30 Sep 2025) includes the extended IJ-geul in its scope, but the TSS lanes are outside the 12 nm VTS sector and the VHF 7 information area has no defined limit. Coverage of the TSS itself is not established. No MRS.
unresolved_issue: Does the VTS area 'including the extended IJ-geul' extend to the adjoining West Outer lanes, and is IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 a defined VTS sector? Check Dutch designation decision or ALRS Vol 6 diagram.

vts_boundary_basis: No Dutch VTS area shown to include the TSS. The statutory aanloopgebied Den Helder (Q-S10) is the Marsdiep sea area bounded by 'grote Kaap' (52°52.9'N 004°42.9'E), buoys SG, ZH, MR, NH, MG and pile 15 on Texel (53°03.7'N 004°43.3'E); the TSS north-eastbound lane's inner boundary lies at 004°17'-004°27.8'E (Q-S12). Buoy positions were not retrieved, so adjacency or overlap is not established; the evidence suggests the approach area lies inshore of the TSS. Coastguard VTMon is monitoring, not VTS (Q-S17, Q-S18).
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). Part of the TSS lies within the Dutch territorial sea (inner lane boundary about 9.5 nm off Texel). STZ art. 5(1) (Q-S10) requires ships of 300 GT or more to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea on a channel designated by ministerial regulation to the competent authority. The designation, receiving authority and practical operation were not found (Q-S11). This is not a named scheme and may be a dormant provision. Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: Off Texel (amended by COLREG.2/Circ.64, 2013) is part of the mandatory tanker route (routeing, not reporting; Q-S14). No Dutch VTS area shown to include it. A statutory territorial-sea entry reporting duty exists on paper (STZ art. 5(1)) but its channel and authority are unconfirmed.
source_date: Q-S10 version 1 Jan 2025; Q-S12 4 Dec 2012; Q-S11 version 27 Mar 2026
unresolved_issue: (1) Positions of Den Helder approach-area buoys SG, ZH, MR, NH, MG versus the TSS. (2) Whether STZ art. 5(1) is operated in practice, on which channel and to which authority (Kustwacht?). Needs the Regeling aanwijzing bevoegde autoriteiten STZ, Dutch Guide to Port Entry or ALRS Vol 6.
vts_coverage_type: As recorded; full/partial extent not standardised
review_note: Current VTS Off Texel identity is confirmed. Earlier no-VTS lead is stale. Exact full/partial overlap and datum reconciliation remain open; no blanket coverage assertion has been substituted.

vts_boundary_basis: No Dutch VTS area shown to include the TSS. The statutory list of Dutch aanloopgebieden (Q-S10) contains no area off Vlieland; the nearest is aanloopgebied Brandaris, 'het zeegat van Terschelling' bounded by buoys Drawa W, ZS, TG and Stolzenfels. Buoy positions were not retrieved. VTMon is monitoring, not VTS (Q-S17).
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). IMO coordinates for B-II/13 were not retrieved, so it is not known whether any part lies in the Dutch territorial sea where STZ art. 5(1) entry reporting would apply (Q-S10); that provision's channel and authority are also unconfirmed. Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: No VTS area covering Off Vlieland found in the statutory Dutch approach-area list; only Kustwacht monitoring. The TSS is subject to the mandatory tanker route (routeing only). MRS status depends on territorial-sea extent, which was not checked.
unresolved_issue: IMO B-II/13 coordinates (not in the opened circulars) to test territorial-sea extent and any overlap with aanloopgebied Brandaris; status of STZ art. 5(1) reporting.

Kustwacht VTMon is monitoring, not VTS (Q-S17, Q-S18). This is not treated as proof of absence because the Dutch VTS designations for offshore waters were not retrieved.

Territorial-sea extent not checked (IMO coordinates not retrieved), so the applicability of STZ art. 5(1) is not resolved. evidence_summary: Offshore Dutch TSS on the northern (mandatory tanker) route. No VTS or MRS association established; only Coastguard monitoring and route advice. The Coastguard's container-ship advice (Q-S19) promotes the northern route but is not a reporting scheme.
unresolved_issue: IMO B-II/13 coordinates; whether any Dutch VTS or reporting duty applies offshore of the approach areas. The Coastguard container-ship advice (Q-S19) directs large container ships to the northern route via TSS East Friesland; whether the MSC 109 recommendation carries any reporting element is not established.
